reasoning_traces.think:
DiffOpt integrates neural motion fields with a motion-diffusion-model (MDM) prior through score-distillation sampling (SDS) to reconstruct global 3D human motion from monocular video. The method uses a three-stage optimization: warm-up to initialize motion fields, camera refinement using DROID-SLAM estimates, and fine-tuning with combined losses. This approach addresses the confounding effect of camera motion on human motion estimation by disentangling both components. However, its single-human scope and test-time optimization make it unsuitable for NFL-scale multi-player tracking. The method’s reliance on pre-trained MDMs and SLAM initialization limits scalability and adaptability to broadcast environments. Its primary contribution lies in global motion accuracy, but lacks practical utility for GSE’s real-time tracking needs.
